Query SAP HANA as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__hana.R
oauth_db_hana.Rd

Read SAP HANA or HANA Cloud data using each visitor's database privileges. HANA checks their signed access token and maps it to a database user. The helper provides a DBI connection for SQL or dbplyr queries.

Usage

oauth_db_hana(
  authorization,
  server,
  database = NULL,
  ...,
  port = 443L,
  schema = NULL,
  driver = "HDBODBC",
  ssl_trust_store = NULL,
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

Function providing the visitor's current sign-in authorization. Pass auth$connection from shinyOAuth without parentheses. To select a saved account, use a function calling auth$connection(id).

server

One HANA SQL endpoint hostname or IPv4 address, without a protocol or port.

database

Optional tenant database name. NULL uses the database selected by the SQL endpoint. HANA Cloud normally needs only its endpoint.

...

Result options timeout, timezone, timezone_out, bigint, encoding, name_encoding, and interruptible. Native authentication, routing, reconnect and TLS settings cannot be overridden.

port

SQL endpoint port, default 443 for HANA Cloud. For self-hosted HANA, use the SQL port supplied by your administrator.

schema

Optional initial SQL schema. NULL uses the user's default.

driver

Installed SAP HANA ODBC driver name, default "HDBODBC", or a library path supported by the driver manager. Install a current SAP HANA Client with JWT authentication support.

ssl_trust_store

Optional trust-store path for the SAP HANA Client's TLS provider. NULL uses the client's configured trust store.

target

Name of the service token to use in your shinyOAuth client. Named targets let one sign-in obtain tokens for different services. NULL uses the client's default token.

required_scopes

Additional OAuth permissions to check before use. Request them on the shinyOAuth client first; this check doesn't request consent or grant database privileges.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

The visitor's Shiny session. Usually inferred when you create the helper inside server().

Value

A reactive function, usually named con. Call connection <- con() inside a render or reactive expression, then pass the connection to DBI. Before sign-in, the function waits quietly.

Details

Install odbc and SAP HANA Client's ODBC driver. Configure HANA to trust your provider's JWT access tokens, map their identities to database users and grant access to the data. The scope and audience depend on that configuration; a SAP BTP browser login alone doesn't establish SQL access.

Create the helper inside server() and call con() before each query. The connection requires encryption and a trusted server certificate. A valid SQL session stays open through ordinary token renewal, with the identity and privileges established when it connected.

Sign-out, account changes or session end close the connection. If it breaks, the next con() reconnects with a current token. The helper doesn't replay a failed query.

See also

vignette("hana", package = "shinyOAuthDB") for sign-in, database configuration and a complete Shiny app.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
con <- oauth_db_hana(
  auth$connection,
  server = "example.hana.prod-eu10.hanacloud.ondemand.com",
  schema = "REPORTING"
)
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT CURRENT_USER AS DATABASE_USER FROM DUMMY")
})
} # }
